page: Microsoft Azure M64-16ms is an x86_64 architecture server within the MS family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8280M processor with 8 physical cores and 16 dedicated vCPUs operating at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The hardware configuration includes a massive memory allocation of 1792.0 GB, yielding 112.0 GB of RAM per core, alongside 2097 GB of local storage.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct performance profile. Single-core CPU performance is limited, with stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded gzip compression all scoring in the bottom 10%. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, reaches average levels. Memory bandwidth tests show average read and write speeds, though the Passmark memory score falls into the bottom 25%.

This server is designed for memory-intensive workloads that require vast RAM capacity but do not demand high single-thread compute performance. The qualitative cost profile reflects a high-density memory allocation paired with a modest CPU configuration, making it suitable for large in-memory databases, caching layers like Redis, and enterprise applications with massive working sets that fit entirely within system memory.
